title: Treat CLASSIFY 0.3.3 as the production-usable baseline
description: Reconciles source-present, contract-published, installed, tested, and graph-complete states before the operator-ergonomics increment.
decision: Current main 777c166 and release 0.3.3 contain the implemented CLASSIFY engine and twelve public operations. The installed Native-AOT executable publishes those operations in a 100-operation inventory, the final module gate records 5609 passing tests, and the owner-local 14-rule evaluation-only rule set has a deterministic 617-row receipt with 146 suggestions, 471 no-suggestions, zero conflicts/stale/canaries, 23.66 percent coverage, and broadApplyAllowed=false. No category allocation was applied. PLAN-CLASSIFY-RULEBOOK-V1 is completed. The remaining problem is bounded operator throughput and discovery, not classifier correctness or autonomous merchant intelligence.
rationale: The prior module narrative described a greenfield implementation and unpublished Ledger projection, which conflicts with current source, released schemas, installed executable evidence, and completed beads.
alternatives: Continue treating CLASSIFY as unbuilt; rejected because it would duplicate shipped code. Treat operator friction as an engine failure; rejected because deterministic evaluation and safety gates passed.
consequences: New work is an additive post-release increment. Historical automatic-discovery failure and owner-rulebook decisions remain intact. Planning and review must test public installed contracts separately from source presence.
